constructionRecord.actuallyRead: Construction, foundations, structure and parking sections; figure13.3 and figure13.5 images actually inspected locally.
findings: Original Capital Hill elevation is reported as RL611.7m; removal was up to21m to the building bench, with basement excavations a further6m below most of the building. The bench was raised1.5m early in excavation. These approximate project-wide statements do not establish an exact absolute forecourt or garage floor level.
Parking for cars and tourist buses is below the forecourt, outside the main parliamentary buildings. Stairs lead up to the forecourt.

The caption to figure13.5 identifies the curved beam as support for the forecourt pool/fountain. Its actual image shows the concrete waffle soffit, curved band beam and columns. It provides construction topology, not measured garage depth.

Figure13.3 shows the longitudinal land-axis section and a flat building bench, with separate horizontal and vertical scales. It is a precinct landform diagram; the garage section and absolute forecourt deck/floor levels are not drawn.
The published early RL583m access constraint belongs to an approach-design alternative discussed in the separate roads chapter; it is not an adopted forecourt slab level.
constructionRecord.modelInspection: Main office masses and curved retaining walls already extend to-18m in the recipe. Only the mapped forecourt has thin slab/surface pieces with no basement shell. Do not describe the whole building as lacking foundations.
constructionRecord.referenceQualification: The old[-7,128]and proposed[45,145]points are dry paved surfaces. Primary sources establish a garage below the forecourt, so a dry paving point must not automatically be treated as bare-earth contact: a DTM value there may represent interpolation below the deck. The exact garage extent still needs its plan. Proposed reference and ACT field remain unadopted.
constructionRecord.remainingEvidence: A verified forecourt garage plan/section and an exterior ground or surveyed level control. A vehicle-clearance number or the project-wide basement excavation depth is not a uniform garage depth.
